speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for your patience. To better understand your condition, could you describe the specific characteristics of the pain in your right knee and the urination episodes? Additionally, have you noticed any skin rashes or eye redness in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your age, recent sexually active history with inconsistent condom use, and the combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (left ankle followed by right knee) with urethritis, I am concerned about Reactive Arthritis. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, and NAAT for Chlamydia trachomatis. Please also return any images of your current knee swelling or any skin rashes.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Protein Negative, Blood Negative, WBC 12–16/hpf, RBC 1–2/hpf. Urine Culture and NAAT for Chlamydia trachomatis: Not provided in current dataset. No images of knee swelling or skin rashes available in current dataset.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; the presence of conjunctivitis alongside your urethritis and asymmetric knee/ankle arthritis strongly supports a diagnosis of Reactive Arthritis. REQUEST TEST: HLA-B27 genetic testing. Do you have any difficulty moving your eyes upward, or does your knee feel warm to the touch? REQUEST IMAGES: Knee X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: HLA-B27 genetic testing: Not provided in current dataset. Difficulty moving eyes upward: Not reported. Knee warmth: The right knee is described as erythematous (red), which clinically correlates with being warm to the touch. Knee X-Ray: Not provided in current dataset.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of asymmetric arthritis, urethritis, and conjunctivitis, along with the erythematous and warm knee, is highly suggestive of Reactive Arthritis. Since we have not yet received your HLA-B27 results or the knee imaging, do you have a history of recent diarrhea or skin infections like a boil before these symptoms started? DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis
